To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a neural network can be used to model the fitness of a genetic algorithm for a particular application and that this fitness model can be used to optimize control parameters for that particular genetic algorithm application.

(1) the neural network based fitness function is a good predictor of the performance of a GA, and (2) the use of this neural network based fitness evaluation can be used to optimize the control parameters of a GA.

the meta-level genetic algorithms are a promising approach to control parameter tuning of the genetic algorithms and that the neural network can be used as a fitness function for the genetic algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods to automatically optimize the control parameters of the genetic algorithm.
the development of genetic algorithms that can be automatically configured for the solution of a problem without requiring human intervention.
the development of genetic algorithms that are capable of self-tuning their own control parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of neural networks in the meta-level genetic optimization of control parameter values for genetic algorithms is a viable approach.
the meta level genetic algorithm approach is a viable and effective approach for the optimization of the control parameter of genetic algorithms.
the neural network approach has proven to be a valuable addition in optimizing the control parameters of a genetic algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a meta-level genetic algorithm can be used to optimize genetic algorithm control parameters, and that this approach can be enhanced using a neural network to predict the performance relative to the values of these control parameter values.

a genetic algorithm can be used to optimize the parameters of a genetic algorithm and the performance of the resulting genetic algorithm will out-perform a genetic algorithm with parameters that are manually optimized.

we have developed a genetic algorithm for a difficult graph problem that is competitive with a hill climbing algorithm used in practical application and that has been shown to be significantly better than a hand tuned version of our genetic algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural network approach can be used to significantly reduce the time and effort needed to tune the parameters of a genetic algorithm.
a genetic algorithm can be used to optimize itself and can be used to develop genetic algorithms that outperform hand-tuned variants.
a genetic algorithm for control parameter optimization is able to outperform a hand-tuned genetic algorithm.
